description:
## Goal

Remove the latent-executable channel from activation analysis because it has no producer and can only publish empty collections. Executable existence must continue to come from its actual root/product ownership path, not from a dormant second vocabulary.

## Proof at a3a9761d1

Every CallEmission construction initializes `latent_executables` to an empty Vec. Merge and rebuild paths only concatenate those empty vectors. Therefore:

- the activation publish loop over call latent executables never emits an Executable fact;
- ActivationAnalysis.latent_executables is always empty;
- dump and telemetry consumers observe only an empty list;
- tests that construct ActivationAnalysis must supply meaningless empty scaffolding.

## Change

- Delete `CallEmission::latent_executables` and `ActivationAnalysis::latent_executables`.
- Delete all empty initializers, merges, rebuild plumbing, and the unreachable publication loop.
- Delete dump, telemetry, and test handling for the field.
- Correct `northstar.html` and agent documentation so AnalyzeActivation publishes only facts it can actually derive.

Do not restore a producer unless a separate semantic requirement identifies an authoritative source, consumer, and exact dependency contract.

## TDD and checks

- `rg latent_executables src tests .agent northstar.html` returns no live-model references.
- Existing root/executable inventory tests prove executable discovery remains unchanged.
- Activation analysis output and causal work are unchanged except for removal of empty data.
- Full library, single-threaded fixture matrix, target fixtures, and clippy with warnings denied pass.

No compatibility field or adapter remains.
title: Delete the always-empty latent-executable channel from activation analysis
